To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

O-GlcNcase over expression in the pancreatic islets results in a decrease in O-GlcNAcylation of proteins in the islets and this decrease is associated with decreased β-cell insulin secretion and decreased islet vascularization, but these defects are overcome with age, resulting in improved β-cell function and islet vascularization.

the O-GlcNcase transgenic mice demonstrate a biphasic effect on glucose tolerance and insulin secretion as a function of aging, with improved β-cell function in older mice associated with increased angiogenic gene expression and islet vascularization.
the effects of O-GlcNcase overexpression on β-cell function and vascularization are pleiotropic and dependent on age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of O-linked glycosylation in the regulation of insulin secretion and islets function and survival in the mouse.
the role of O-GlcNac in the maintenance of pancreatic β-cell function and vascularization and its role in diabetes.
the regulation of O-GlcNac signaling in the pancreatic β cell and its role in the maintenance of normal glucose homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
decreased protein O-GlcNAcylation in the pancreatic β cell is associated with age-dependent effects on β-cell function, insulin content, angiogenesis, and VEGF expression.
the effect of decreased O-linked N-acetylgucosamine (OGlcNAc) on β-cell function and survival is age-dependent.
O-GlcNac is a key regulator of β-cell function and survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the O-GlcNacylation pathway is an important regulator of β-cell function, and its dysregulation is a contributing factor in the pathogenesis of diabetes.
O-linked N-acetylglycosylation (O-GlcNac) is important for the maintenance of pancreatic β-cell function.
the O-GlcNcase transgenic mice demonstrate that O-Glcnac signaling has both positive and negative effects on the function and vascularization of β cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
decreased O-GlcNacylation of β-cell proteins is detrimental to normal β-cell function and that the detrimental effects are reversible with aging.
O-GlcNac signaling plays a role in β-cell maintenance and that O-Glc-NAcase may be a useful therapeutic agent in the prevention of diabetes.
decreased O-GlcNc in the β-cell can have both beneficial and detrimental effects on β-cell function and survival.
